[00:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Right. Let me start with numbers and then you tell me what I've missed. You're fourteen months in. Twenty-two workflows in production, up from six at the end of the first quarter. Run volume's roughly two hundred and eighty thousand a month.
[00:41] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): That sounds about right.
[00:43] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Error rate's sitting at one point four percent, which is down from four point one when you started. Most of that improvement came in April.
[00:53] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): April was when we fixed the store-data validation. That was our fault, not yours.
[01:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I know, but it counts.
[01:03] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): What I care about is the depot exceptions workflow. Can you give me that one specifically?
[01:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Yes. Median time from exception raised to first action is now forty minutes. It was — Devan, what was it before?
[01:20] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Between two and six hours, depending on who was on.
[01:24] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Six hours was optimistic.
[01:27] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [laughs] Six hours was the number we admitted to.
[01:31] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): That's the one that's changed how the depots work. Genuinely. I had a depot manager tell me in July that he'd stopped keeping his own spreadsheet, and that's — you don't get that often.
[01:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the metric I'd actually put in front of your board, for what it's worth. Not the run counts.
[01:54] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): I already have.
[01:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Good. Now the less pleasant part of the numbers.
[02:02] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Overages.
[02:03] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Overages. You've exceeded your contracted run volume in four of the last six months. June was twenty-two percent over.
[02:13] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): We knew. We've been watching it.
[02:16] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Were we charged for those?
[02:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You were charged for two of them. Two were waived — one in March because it was a retry storm caused by a Salesforce outage on their side, and one in May which I waived because you'd flagged it to us proactively before the invoice.
[02:37] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): I didn't know that.
[02:39] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): I knew about March. I didn't know about May.
[02:43] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): May was a judgement call. I'd rather tell you now than have it look like a discovery in the renewal.
[02:51] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Appreciated. But it does mean the run tier is wrong.
[02:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The run tier is wrong, yes. Which is most of what I want to talk about.
[03:02] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Can I ask something before we get to money?
[03:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[03:08] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): The retry storm in March. Has anything changed at your end so that doesn't happen again? Because from our side we did nothing wrong and it cost us twenty thousand runs.
[03:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Partly. There are retry controls and you can set caps per workflow, and we can look at whether yours are configured sensibly — I suspect two or three of them aren't. But if a downstream system is down for six hours and your workflows keep firing, you will burn runs.
[03:43] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): So the answer is configure it better.
[03:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): The answer is configure it better, and I should have done that with you in April rather than now. That's on me.
[03:56] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] Alright.
[03:58] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Can we book that as a session rather than an action item that dies?
[04:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Yes. I'll put an hour in with Devan for the fortnight after next.
[04:10] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Fine.
[04:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Adoption. This is the bit I want to push on. You've got nine builders licensed and four of them haven't published anything in six months.
[04:23] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Two of those have moved teams.
[04:26] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then we should take them off, not keep paying for them.
[04:31] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): You're offering to reduce our seat count?
[04:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'm telling you what the data says. Maya may have a different view.
[04:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I have exactly the same view. Nine licensed builders with four dormant is a renewal that gets scrutinised. I'd rather sell you seven active seats and a higher run tier than nine seats where four are indefensible.
[04:57] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): That's — okay. That's a more sensible conversation than I was braced for.
[05:04] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Braced for what?
[05:06] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Braced for "here's a fifteen percent uplift, sign here."
[05:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): There is an uplift. I'll come to it.
[05:15] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): [laughs] Of course there is.
[05:18] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Let me finish the review first, because there's an expansion question and I think it changes the shape of the commercial conversation.
[05:27] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Go on.
[05:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You mentioned in July you were thinking about the supplier onboarding process.
[05:35] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Devan, do you want to?
[05:37] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): So — at the moment, bringing on a new supplier involves about nine handoffs between buying, compliance, finance and the depot systems team. It's email and a SharePoint list.
[05:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): How long?
[05:54] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Target's fifteen working days. Actual is somewhere around thirty.
[05:59] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Thirty-four last quarter.
[06:02] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Thirty-four. And the buying team is now blaming compliance and compliance is blaming the depot systems team, and honestly they're all a bit right.
[06:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Is that a workflow problem or an organisational problem?
[06:18] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] That's a good question.
[06:21] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): It's both, but I'd say the reason it's an organisational problem is that nobody can see where it's stuck. If you could see it, the arguing would stop.
[06:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's usually true. I'd flag one risk though — if the process itself is genuinely broken, automating it makes it a faster broken process.
[06:45] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): We've said that internally.
[06:48] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Compliance said it, and they said it loudly.
[06:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then I'd suggest the first phase is visibility only. Don't automate the handoffs. Just instrument them — track where a supplier onboarding is, who has it, how long they've had it. Run that for six weeks and look at the data.
[07:11] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): And then automate.
[07:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And then automate the bits the data says are actually the problem, rather than the bits people complain loudest about. Those are usually different.
[07:24] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): That's cheaper too.
[07:26] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's cheaper and it's much easier to get compliance to agree to.
[07:31] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] Yes. Let's do that.
[07:35] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Would that be a lot of runs?
[07:38] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): No. Instrumentation is light — you're recording state transitions, not orchestrating them. Maybe a few thousand a month.
[07:48] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): That's nothing.
[07:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's nothing. The expensive phase is later.
[07:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is relevant to how I structure the renewal, actually.
[07:59] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Go on then. Let's do it.
[08:02] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Current contract is Enterprise, nine builder seats, run tier at two hundred and fifty thousand a month. It expires the eighteenth of October.
[08:14] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Six weeks.
[08:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Six weeks, which is why I wanted this conversation now rather than in October.
[08:22] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): What's the uplift?
[08:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): List uplift at renewal is seven percent. That's the standard annual adjustment and I'm not going to pretend it's negotiable in principle — it applies to everyone.
[08:36] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Seven. Not fifteen.
[08:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Seven.
[08:41] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): That's more reasonable than I expected.
[08:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): But the run tier change is a bigger number than the uplift, and I want to be upfront about that. You need three hundred and fifty thousand, not two fifty, and that's before the supplier onboarding work.
[08:59] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Three fifty gives us headroom?
[09:02] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Three fifty gives you about twenty percent headroom on your current trajectory. Four hundred gives you a year and the instrumentation project.
[09:12] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): What's the delta between three fifty and four hundred?
[09:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll send exact numbers, but roughly — the step from two fifty to three fifty is the significant one. Three fifty to four hundred is a smaller increment because of how the tiers are shaped.
[09:31] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): So we should take four hundred.
[09:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I think you should take four hundred, and I'd rather say that than sell you three fifty and have this conversation again in May.
[09:43] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): What's the total? Directionally.
[09:46] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Directionally, with seven seats instead of nine, seven percent uplift, and the four hundred thousand tier — you're looking at roughly nine percent above what you paid this year. If we kept nine seats it'd be closer to fourteen.
[10:04] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] Nine percent for forty percent more capacity and a new use case.
[10:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the shape of it. And I want to be clear that the seat reduction is genuine — I'm not inflating the run tier to compensate.
[10:21] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Can you show that? The two things separately?
[10:25] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes, and I'll show last year's line items next to next year's so you can see exactly what moved.
[10:33] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Please. That's the thing that gets a renewal signed here — I have to take it to a finance director who will ask what changed and why.
[10:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then it'll be built for that conversation rather than for this one.
[10:49] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): What about multi-year? Is there anything in it for us?
[10:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): There is. A two-year commitment lets me fix the uplift for year two, which given where inflation's gone is probably worth more than the discount itself.
[11:06] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): How much discount?
[11:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd need to model it properly. I'd be guessing if I said a number now and I'd rather not guess at a renewal.
[11:16] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Would you do three years?
[11:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd do three. Should you? Probably not.
[11:23] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Why not?
[11:25] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Because you're fourteen months into a platform that's going well, and three years is a long commitment for something you haven't yet used for the harder use case. If supplier onboarding goes badly you'd be locked into a tier you don't need. Two years is where I'd sit.
[11:45] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): That's an odd thing for you to say.
[11:48] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's a very normal thing for me to say to a customer I want to renew four times rather than once.
[11:56] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Alright. Model two years, and model three so I can see it, and I'll decide.
[12:03] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Done.
[12:05] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can I raise the support thing while we're here?
[12:09] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Yes, please do, because Devan's been complaining.
[12:13] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): I have been complaining.
[12:15] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Say it.
[12:17] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Response times have been fine. Resolution times on anything involving the SAP connector have been terrible. We had a ticket open for nineteen days in July.
[12:30] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I looked at that one before this call. It went to second line, then to engineering, then it sat.
[12:38] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): It sat for eleven days.
[12:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It sat for eleven days and there's no good explanation. I've raised it internally and the honest answer I got was that it fell between two teams.
[12:53] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): That's what it looked like from outside.
[12:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What I can do is name a specific engineer as the escalation contact for SAP issues on your account. What I can't do is promise you a resolution SLA on connector defects, because we don't offer one and I'm not going to invent it at a renewal.
[13:16] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] The named contact is more useful than a promise, honestly.
[13:22] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Is it worth putting anything in the contract?
[13:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Your Enterprise agreement already includes priority support with response-time commitments. Resolution-time commitments are a different thing and we don't do them. If someone tells you otherwise, check the paper.
[13:41] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Noted.
[13:43] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): One more from my side and then I'll let you go. Governance.
[13:48] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Mm.
[13:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You've got twenty-two production workflows and your naming convention has drifted. There are four called some variant of "depot exception" and I genuinely could not tell you which is live.
[14:04] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Two are live. One's a test that should have been deleted. One's the old version.
[14:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can you delete them?
[14:13] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): I can delete the test. The old version I'd want to keep for a bit.
[14:19] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then rename it. "Deprecated" in the name, and set it inactive.
[14:25] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Fine.
[14:27] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'm being pedantic because this is exactly how you end up in three years with forty workflows and nobody knowing which matter. I've seen it.
[14:38] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): We came from that. That was the Zapier estate.
[14:43] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Sixty-odd Zaps, half of them orphaned.
[14:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then you know.
[14:49] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): We know. It's just that tidying isn't urgent until it is.
[14:55] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's never urgent. That's the problem with it.
[15:00] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Put it on the list, Devan.
[15:03] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): It's on the list.
[15:05] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll check in December.
[15:07] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [laughs] I'm sure you will.
[15:11] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Can I ask about something unrelated?
[15:14] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Of course.
[15:16] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): The AI features. We've never turned them on. Should we?
[15:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What would you want them for?
[15:25] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): I don't know. That's why I'm asking. There's pressure from above to have an AI story and I'd rather have a real one than a made-up one.
[15:36] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Then my honest answer is: don't turn them on because there's pressure. Turn them on when there's a task where the input is genuinely unstructured.
[15:48] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Is there one?
[15:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Possibly. The depot exception free-text field — Devan, how much gets typed into that?
[15:58] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): A lot. It's the field where people explain what actually happened.
[16:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then categorising those into themes so Fiona can see what's recurring across depots — that's a real use, and it's low risk because nobody's making a decision from it directly.
[16:19] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): That would be genuinely useful actually.
[16:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): With one condition. The output has to link back to the underlying exceptions so someone can check it. If it says "forty percent of exceptions relate to chilled goods handling", you need to be able to click through to the forty percent.
[16:39] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Otherwise it's a made-up number.
[16:42] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Otherwise it's a plausible number, which is worse.
[16:46] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Does that need Enterprise? We're on Enterprise anyway.
[16:51] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You're on Enterprise, so you have the controls — restricting which models are allowed, disabling it per workspace, the model configuration logged per run. You'd want to talk to your security people before switching it on, but it's a conversation rather than a project.
[17:11] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Who's our security person?
[17:13] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Priyanka. She'll want the subprocessor list.
[17:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll send it. And the statement that we don't use customer workflow content to train a shared model — she'll ask for that and it's in your contract already.
[17:29] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Is it? I didn't know that.
[17:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's clause fourteen. It went in at the original signature because your legal team asked for it.
[17:39] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Good for them.
[17:41] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Right. What are we agreeing today?
[17:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Nothing binding. What you'll get from me by Friday is the renewal proposal with last year's line items next to next year's, seven seats, four hundred thousand runs, and one-year, two-year and three-year options priced separately.
[18:03] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): And the seat reduction is in there.
[18:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The seat reduction is in there and it's called out explicitly so your finance director can see it.
[18:13] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Good.
[18:15] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): From me — the retry configuration session with Devan, the subprocessor list for Priyanka, a short note on what the supplier onboarding instrumentation phase would look like, and the named SAP escalation contact.
[18:32] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): When for the escalation contact?
[18:35] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): This week. That one's easy.
[18:38] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Alright.
[18:40] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): And we owe you what?
[18:42] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): A decision on whether supplier onboarding instrumentation happens this side of Christmas, because it affects whether four hundred thousand is the right tier. And Devan owes me some deleted workflows.
[18:56] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): I'll delete the test one today.
[18:59] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): On the renewal — realistically I'll come back to you the week of the fifteenth. I need to get it in front of finance and they meet fortnightly.
[19:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's fine and it's within the window. If it slips past the eighteenth we can bridge it, but I'd rather not because bridging always creates a mess in someone's system.
[19:24] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): It won't slip.
[19:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask a question that isn't about the renewal?
[19:31] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Go on.
[19:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What's the thing we do that you'd miss most if it vanished tomorrow?
[19:39] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): [pause] The depot exception routing. Without question. Everything else we could go back to doing the old way and survive. That one has changed the operating rhythm and going back would be genuinely painful.
[19:56] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): I'd say the run history, personally. But I'm not the business.
[20:02] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why the run history?
[20:04] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Because when something breaks I can answer the question in four minutes instead of half a day. That's not visible to Fiona but it's most of my quality of life.
[20:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's useful to hear, genuinely. It's the thing we're worst at explaining in a sales conversation.
[20:25] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): It's not exciting.
[20:27] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's not exciting until it's three in the morning.
[20:31] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): [laughs] It has been three in the morning.
[20:35] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Right, I've got a store visit. Ruth, thank you, this was useful. Maya, send the numbers.
[20:43] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Friday.
[20:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Thanks both. Devan, I'll get that session in the diary.
[20:50] Devan Shah (Platform Manager, Lumen Retail Group): Cheers. Bye.
[20:52] Fiona Bright (Head of Retail Operations, Lumen Retail Group): Bye.

context.text:
=== CALL-012 (call kind: renewal)
CALL ID: CALL-012
DATE: 2026-09-08
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Pinewood Insurance
INDUSTRY: Insurance
COMPANY SIZE: 1,400 employees
STAGE: Renewal / at risk
DURATION: 23 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Leo Grant, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Graham Attwood, Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance
- Nadia Rahman, IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Morning Graham, morning Nadia. Thanks for making the time — I know this one's been rescheduled twice.
[00:08] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Three times, I think. That's on us.
[00:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I wasn't counting.
[00:14] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): You were, but that's fine.
[00:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [laughs] Slightly. Look, I want to be direct about why I asked for this. Your renewal's on the twenty-ninth of November. Usage has dropped about forty percent since March. And I've had two conversations with Nadia that suggested you're not happy. I'd rather have the awkward conversation now than a surprise in November.
[00:41] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): That's fair.
[00:43] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): It's also accurate.
[00:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then tell me. Start wherever you want.
[00:50] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): The honest answer is that I inherited this. Ravi bought it, Ravi implemented it, Ravi left in February, and I picked it up in March with about forty minutes of handover.
[01:05] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Forty minutes.
[01:07] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Forty minutes and a Confluence page that was last edited in November.
[01:13] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): The Confluence page is quite good, in fairness.
[01:17] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): The Confluence page is the only reason anything still works.
[01:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a failure on our side too. When your named champion leaves, we should be re-onboarding whoever picks it up, and nobody did that.
[01:33] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): No, nobody did.
[01:35] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I took over your account in May. It should have been the first thing I did and it wasn't.
[01:42] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] I appreciate you saying that rather than telling me about a training portal.
[01:49] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): There is a training portal.
[01:51] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I know there is. I've never opened it.
[01:54] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Nobody opens it.
[01:56] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): [laughs]
[01:58] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Let me put the numbers up and you tell me what they mean from where you sit. You've got fourteen workflows in production. Six of them haven't run successfully in the last ninety days.
[02:12] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Which six?
[02:14] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll send the list, but broadly — three are the claims triage set, two are broker onboarding, and one is something called "TEMP - do not use" which has been running on a schedule since January.
[02:29] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] It's been running since January?
[02:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's been failing since January. Every four hours.
[02:38] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Nobody told us.
[02:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You'd have got the failure alerts. They're going to Ravi's address, which still exists as a shared mailbox that nobody reads.
[02:50] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Oh, for goodness' sake.
[02:53] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): That's — yeah. That's on us.
[02:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's on both of us. You should have redirected the alerts. We should have noticed a workflow failing two thousand times and rung someone.
[03:07] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Do you not monitor that?
[03:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Not proactively at your account tier, no. And I'd rather tell you that plainly than imply we're watching when we aren't.
[03:20] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] Right.
[03:22] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Is that something you do at a higher tier?
[03:26] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): There's more proactive review on the largest accounts. It's not a product feature you can buy, it's how our team allocates time, and I don't want to dress that up as something it isn't.
[03:40] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I'd rather know.
[03:42] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): The three claims triage ones concern me more than the temp one. Those were the reason you bought.
[03:50] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): They were the reason Ravi bought.
[03:53] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Are they still the reason?
[03:56] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] I don't know. That's the honest answer. The claims director changed in April and the new one has a different view about where triage should happen.
[04:09] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): She wants it in Guidewire.
[04:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Ah.
[04:14] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): She wants it in Guidewire, and she has a point, because that's where the claims handlers already are.
[04:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a legitimate architectural position and I'm not going to argue against it. Can Guidewire do the cross-system part? The bit that pulls from the broker portal and the document store?
[04:36] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Not natively. That's what we'd have to build.
[04:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): With what?
[04:43] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Power Automate, probably. Or Guidewire's own integration layer, which our vendor tells us is capable and our developers tell me is painful.
[04:55] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which do you believe?
[04:58] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): [laughs] The developers. Always the developers.
[05:03] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): So the situation is that half of what we bought this for might move somewhere else, and the other half — broker onboarding — is stalled for a completely different reason.
[05:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which is?
[05:18] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Nobody's building anything. We've got four builder licences. One person uses it. She's brilliant, she's called Ellie, and she's been on maternity leave since June.
[05:32] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you have a bus factor of one and the bus arrived.
[05:37] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): The bus arrived, yes.
[05:40] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): We tried to get two people up to speed in July. It didn't take.
[05:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Why not?
[05:48] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): They're busy. And the learning curve for the first workflow is steeper than the marketing suggests.
[05:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): How steep?
[05:58] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): One of them spent two days on it and produced something that didn't work, and then went back to their actual job. Which I entirely understand.
[06:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did they ask for help?
[06:12] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): No.
[06:14] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Would they have known who to ask?
[06:17] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] Probably not.
[06:20] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the bit I can actually fix.
[06:23] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Can you?
[06:25] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Some of it. Enablement sessions, office hours, a named contact. What I can't fix is that your people are busy and this isn't their day job. If the only person who ever built anything was Ellie, then when Ellie's not here you have a very expensive product that nobody operates.
[06:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): That's precisely the position I'm in.
[06:51] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I come in?
[06:53] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Please.
[06:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've been listening and I want to say something that probably isn't in my interest. You're on Enterprise. Looking at what you're actually using, I'm not sure you should be.
[07:08] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Go on.
[07:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Enterprise gives you SAML SSO and SCIM, EU data residency, audit export, advanced workspace governance, the ability to disable AI features, priority support. Nadia, how many of those are you using?
[07:27] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): SSO, obviously. Audit export — no. Residency — we're UK only and we're on the EU region, so, technically yes, but it's not a requirement anyone's written down.
[07:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Advanced workspace governance?
[07:44] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): We have one workspace.
[07:46] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right.
[07:48] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): What's the alternative?
[07:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Growth. Eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, annual. You'd lose SCIM, audit export, EU residency as a contractual commitment, some of the governance controls, and priority support drops to standard.
[08:07] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): We'd lose SSO?
[08:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): SAML SSO is Enterprise. So yes, that's the one that would actually hurt.
[08:16] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): That's a problem. Our security standard requires SSO for anything holding claims data.
[08:24] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then Growth isn't viable and I've just talked myself out of my own suggestion.
[08:30] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [laughs] That was quick.
[08:33] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's better to find out now. But it does mean the question is different — it's not "which tier", it's "is Enterprise worth it for what you're getting", and right now the honest answer is probably not, because you're getting very little.
[08:50] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): So what do you suggest?
[08:53] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Two options and I'll be straight about both. Option one, you don't renew. We part on good terms, you export your workflow definitions and run data, and if the Guidewire route works out you were right.
[09:09] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): You're offering me that?
[09:11] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather offer it than have you sign a renewal you resent and churn next year with a bad taste.
[09:19] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): What's option two?
[09:21] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Option two is a shorter renewal with a genuine re-implementation attached. Six months rather than twelve, with a defined enablement programme, and we agree measurable criteria at the start. If it works, you renew properly in May. If it doesn't, you leave in May and you've spent six months' fees finding out rather than twelve.
[09:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Would you discount six months?
[09:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Six months at the annual rate pro-rata, not at a short-term premium. So no uplift, no penalty for the shorter term. That's the concession.
[10:02] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): And what would the enablement look like? Because "we'll do some training" is not going to convince my finance director.
[10:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Let me answer that, because it's mine. It'd be four things. First, re-onboarding for you and Nadia specifically — not the training portal, a working session on what you actually own. Second, three builders trained properly, and I mean sitting with them while they build a real workflow, not a demo one.
[10:35] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Which three?
[10:37] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You'd pick. But I'd want commitment from their managers that they get the time, in writing, because otherwise it's July again.
[10:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): That's a reasonable ask.
[10:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Third, we fix the estate. Delete the temp workflow, redirect the alerts away from Ravi's mailbox, review the six that are failing and decide for each one whether to fix it or kill it. I'd guess three should be killed.
[11:08] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Probably four.
[11:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Probably four. And fourth — we settle the Guidewire question rather than leaving it hanging, because if claims triage is moving, then the case for this product rests entirely on broker onboarding and you should know that before you renew anything.
[11:29] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): How would we settle it?
[11:32] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Get the claims director in a room with Nadia and have the cross-system conversation. Not with me in the room — this isn't a vendor question.
[11:44] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] That's the right answer and I've been avoiding it.
[11:50] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): We've both been avoiding it.
[11:53] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Because she'll win.
[11:55] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): She might win.
[11:57] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): She'll win on claims and she should. The question is whether she wins on everything.
[12:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then that's the meeting to have. And whichever way it goes, you'd know what you're buying.
[12:11] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Can I ask something blunt?
[12:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[12:16] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): If we do option two and it doesn't work, do you actually let us leave in May, or does it become a negotiation?
[12:25] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's a six-month term. It ends. There's no auto-renew clause on a term like that and I'd put that in writing.
[12:34] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Because our current contract does auto-renew.
[12:38] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Your current contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, which means your notice deadline is the thirtieth of September.
[12:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] Three weeks.
[12:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Three weeks.
[12:52] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Did you know that, Graham?
[12:54] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I did not know that.
[12:57] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is why I've said it now rather than on the first of October. I'm not going to auto-renew you into a twelve-month contract you didn't intend to sign.
[13:08] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Some vendors would.
[13:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Some vendors do. It's a terrible way to run a business.
[13:15] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] Right. So I need to serve notice by the thirtieth regardless, to keep my options open.
[13:24] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd suggest you do exactly that. Serve notice, which stops the auto-renew, and then we negotiate the six-month option separately without a clock on it. That's the cleanest thing for you.
[13:39] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): You're telling us to serve notice on our own contract.
[13:44] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'm telling you to preserve your optionality. If you serve notice and then decide to do the six months, that's a new agreement and everyone knows what they're signing.
[13:56] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Ruth, is he allowed to say this?
[13:59] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [laughs] He's said worse.
[14:02] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have a customer in May than a lawsuit in March.
[14:07] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Nobody's suing anybody.
[14:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No, but you'd be annoyed, and annoyed customers tell other people.
[14:15] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): That's more honest than I expected.
[14:18] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Can I raise the support thing? Since we're being honest.
[14:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Please.
[14:25] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): We've raised eleven tickets this year. Four of them we closed ourselves because we'd worked it out before anyone came back.
[14:35] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What was the response time?
[14:38] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Within SLA, technically. But "within SLA" was a message asking us to confirm details we'd already provided in the ticket.
[14:48] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a real complaint and I've heard it before.
[14:52] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): It's not catastrophic. It's just — it's the kind of thing that means I don't raise tickets any more, and then you look at the data and conclude we're happy.
[15:04] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's a very good point and it's slightly chilling.
[15:09] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Low ticket volume can mean two things.
[15:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Low ticket volume can mean two things, yes. I'll be more careful with that metric.
[15:19] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): What would you actually change?
[15:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For the six months, I'd want a fortnightly fifteen-minute call with Nadia. Not a QBR. Fifteen minutes, what's broken, what's annoying, what's stuck. Most of what she's described would have surfaced in the first one.
[15:39] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): I'd do that. Fifteen minutes I can do.
[15:43] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): An hour a month I can't argue with.
[15:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Half an hour a month.
[15:48] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Even better.
[15:51] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I put some numbers on option two so you've got something concrete?
[15:56] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Please.
[15:58] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Six months at your current annual rate pro-rata. Four builder seats, unchanged — I'd keep four rather than cut to three, because the whole point is getting more people building. Run tier unchanged, you're nowhere near it. Enablement included, not charged as professional services.
[16:19] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Included?
[16:21] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Included. If I charge you for enablement to fix an adoption problem we partly caused, you'd be right to tell me to go away.
[16:31] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): What's that worth, roughly?
[16:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Three properly trained builders is about four days of someone's time. I'd have to check what we'd normally charge.
[16:43] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We'd normally charge for it. I'd rather not.
[16:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): And the criteria? You said measurable criteria.
[16:51] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You'd write them, not me. But if I were you I'd want something like — three people other than Ellie have each built and shipped a production workflow. The failing six are resolved or deleted. The Guidewire question is settled and documented. And broker onboarding cycle time has moved, or you know why it hasn't.
[17:16] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Those are all measurable.
[17:19] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): The Guidewire one isn't a metric.
[17:22] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No, it's a decision. But it's binary and it's got a date, which is close enough.
[17:29] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): What happens if we hit three of four?
[17:33] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then you decide. I'm not going to pre-commit to a rule about it. If three of four have landed and the fourth is in progress, you'll know whether it's working.
[17:45] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Hm.
[17:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can I add something? The one I'd weight most heavily is the first one. Three people other than Ellie shipping something real. If that happens, everything else is solvable. If it doesn't happen, nothing else matters and you should leave.
[18:05] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): That's a clear statement.
[18:08] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's the actual test. All the other stuff is symptoms.
[18:13] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Ellie's back in November, incidentally.
[18:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's helpful and it's also a trap.
[18:20] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Because she'll just do it all again.
[18:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Because she'll do it all again and you'll be back here in a year with a bus factor of one. I'd almost rather do the enablement before she's back.
[18:34] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [pause] That's a good point.
[18:37] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): October, then.
[18:39] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): October would be ideal.
[18:42] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Let me tell you where I am. I'm not going to pretend I'm enthusiastic. If you'd asked me two weeks ago I'd have said we're not renewing.
[18:53] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What's changed?

And the honest position — that we're paying for Enterprise and getting very little — matches what I'd concluded myself, which is reassuring.
[19:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd still say there's a real chance you shouldn't renew.
[19:19] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I know. That's rather the point.
[19:22] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): My concern is different. I don't think the product is the problem. I think we implemented it badly, one person owned it, and then she left and then the other one went on leave. That's an us problem.
[19:37] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's partly an us problem. A product that only one person in an organisation can use is a product with an onboarding failure, and that's ours.
[19:49] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): That's generous.
[19:51] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's not generous, it's true. If we needed Ellie to be exceptional, that's a design problem.
[19:59] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Right. Next steps. What do I need to do by the thirtieth?
[20:05] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Serve notice. It's an email to your account contact, and I'll send you the exact wording and address so it's unambiguous. That stops the auto-renew and costs you nothing.
[20:19] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): And then?
[20:21] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then we have three weeks in October to agree the six-month terms, or you let it lapse on the twenty-ninth of November. Either is a legitimate outcome.
[20:33] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Send me the six-month proposal too, so I can put both in front of finance at the same time.
[20:40] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll send both by Thursday. The proposal, and a one-page comparison of renew-six-months versus lapse, with what you'd lose in each case.
[20:52] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): You'll write the case for lapsing?
[20:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll write it accurately. You can decide whether it's compelling.
[21:00] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [laughs] Alright.
[21:03] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): From me — the list of the six failing workflows today, the alert redirection instructions today, and I'll draft what the enablement programme would look like with specific dates rather than a description.
[21:19] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Can you send the export instructions as well?
[21:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For your definitions and run data? Yes.
[21:27] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Regardless of what we decide.
[21:30] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Regardless of what you decide. You should have that anyway and it shouldn't be a leaving-related request.
[21:38] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): And I'll get the meeting with the claims director. I'll do it next week.
[21:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the one that matters most.
[21:47] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I know. I've known for four months.
[21:51] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): Five.
[21:52] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): [crosstalk] Five. Thank you, Nadia.
[21:55] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): [laughs] Sorry.
[21:58] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): One last thing and then I'll let you go. If you do lapse — and I mean this — tell us why properly. Not a form. An actual conversation. [22:23] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): I'd do that.
[22:25] Nadia Rahman (IT Service Owner, Pinewood Insurance): I'd enjoy that, honestly.
[22:28] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [laughs] I'm sure you would.
[22:31] Graham Attwood (Director of Operations, Pinewood Insurance): Right. Thank you both. That was more useful than I expected and I say that having dreaded it.
[22:39] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks Graham. Thursday for the papers.

[21:26] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): There is a second use case I should mention, not for phase one.
[21:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[21:34] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Replacing several departmental Python scripts with centrally visible automations and approvals. The four-year-old script Anika mentioned is not unique. We think there are — Anika, what was the estimate?
[21:51] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): We identified thirty-one. We believe there are more.
[21:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thirty-one that you know about.
[21:59] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Thirty-one that we know about. Yes.
[22:03] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's a genuinely good second-phase use case, and I'd note it's a different kind of value than the first one. The first one is cycle time. This one is risk reduction and auditability.
[22:19] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): For me it is the more interesting one.
[22:23] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): For finance it is the less interesting one, which is why it is phase two.
[22:29] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): [laughs] That is accurate.
[22:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd argue you can put a number on it. Not savings — avoided incident cost. But that's a harder internal sell and I wouldn't lead with it.
[22:45] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): No. Lead with cycle time.
[22:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Environment separation — you'd flagged wanting separate developer, test and production workspaces with change control.
[22:58] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That is not negotiable. We do not put anything into production that has not been through test, and we do not let the person who built something be the only person who approves it.
[23:12] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Workspace separation is supported and Enterprise has stronger governance around who can publish where. There's version history and change metadata on every workflow. Rollback and promotion patterns vary a bit depending on the workflow and the package, and I'd want to walk through your specific promotion process rather than assume it maps.
[23:37] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Our promotion process is documented. I will send it.
[23:42] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then I'll map it against what the platform does and tell you where the gaps are. There will be gaps — there always are — the question is whether they're gaps you can live with.
[23:56] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I would also like the change-management scenario included in any evaluation. Not just "build the workflow." Build it, change it, break it, roll it back.
[24:10] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's a better evaluation than most customers design. Yes.
[24:16] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Anika designs our evaluations.
[24:19] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Somebody has to.
[24:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask about naming and standards? You mentioned governance of local scripts. What would you want in place before business teams start building?
[24:34] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Naming conventions. Change control for anything classified as important. A rule that somebody other than the creator can understand each production workflow. And a register — I want to be able to answer the question "how many automations do we have" without a discovery project.
[24:56] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That matches our recommended operating model almost exactly. A few centrally owned templates, defined publishing rights, dev separated from prod, and a small central group owning standards while business teams contribute requirements.
[25:15] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Who does that in practice at your other customers? A team? A person?
[25:22] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Usually a small team, two to four people, sitting in whatever function is closest to the process. Sometimes IT, more often operations. The pattern that fails is when it's one person's side project.
[25:39] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): We have a lot of one-person side projects.
[25:43] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I know. That's why I mention it.
[25:47] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I have twelve minutes. Can we do the AI question? Because I have a position on it and I would rather state it than have it discovered.
[25:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[26:00] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): My position is that I do not want generative AI in the first phase at all. Not because I object in principle. Because it adds a review process — data protection, works council, possibly legal — and I do not want that review sitting on the critical path of a project whose value comes from something else entirely.
[26:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a strategically sound position and I'm not going to argue with it.
[26:32] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I expected you to argue with it.
[26:35] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The product is a workflow platform. AI steps are optional steps inside a workflow, not the substance of it. If you turn them off, you have a workflow platform. That's fine.
[26:50] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): And to be concrete — Enterprise customers can disable AI features. Administrators can restrict which models are allowed. AI steps are explicit, inspectable workflow steps rather than something ambient. We log the model configuration used on a run. And we don't use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model.
[27:16] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That last point needs to be contractual.
[27:20] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It should be, and you should insist on it.
[27:24] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I will.
[27:27] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Anika, before you go — is there anything on your list we have not covered?
[27:33] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Two things. First, can audit data be exported to our own systems? We do not accept a vendor console as an audit trail.
[27:45] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Run events and metrics through APIs and webhooks, and audit export on Enterprise. Several customers forward failures into their incident tooling.
[27:57] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Then that is satisfactory. Second — data deletion. If we terminate, what happens?
[28:06] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's a contractual and configuration question and I'd rather it be answered in writing by someone who can commit to it. I'll flag it for the pack.
[28:18] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Good. Then I am finished. Martin, you have my notes. Thank you both.
[28:25] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thank you, Anika. That was genuinely useful.
[28:29] Anika Bose (IT Governance Lead, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): [inaudible] — goodbye.
[28:33] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): She is very thorough.
[28:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): She's the most organised governance lead I've spoken to this year and I mean that.
[28:43] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): She will be pleased. I will not tell her.
[28:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] Understood.
[28:51] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Can I ask you something slightly off topic?
[28:55] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Of course.
[28:57] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Were you at Hannover Messe in April?
[29:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I wasn't, no. Jon?
[29:04] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): No. I've been to it once, years ago, in a previous job. It is enormous.
[29:11] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): It is enormous and it is exhausting. I ask because I spoke to a workflow vendor there and I cannot remember which one, and it has been irritating me for two months.
[29:24] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): If they had an orange stand it wasn't us.
[29:28] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): [laughs] I don't remember the colour.
[29:32] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then it definitely wasn't us. Nobody forgets our stand, we spend far too much on it.
[29:39] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Well. If I remember I will tell you and you can tell me what is wrong with them.
[29:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd be delighted.
[29:48] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Shall we do the remaining part? I have until the hour.
[29:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes. I want to cover ROI, the decision process, and timing, and then I want to ask you a direct question about next steps.

[30:12] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Not headcount. I want to be very clear about that because in a manufacturing business the word automation makes people nervous for reasons that have nothing to do with software.
[30:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood.
[30:28] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): The case is cycle time and error reduction. [30:52] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We hear that in every industry, and nobody has a number for it.
[30:57] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Because to get the number you have to admit how much time you spend on it.

[31:24] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Elapsed time and exception rate. Those we can measure.
[31:29] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And I'd add adoption. A technically correct workflow that everyone routes around is a failed implementation.
[31:37] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): We have a museum of technically correct systems.
[31:41] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] Most large companies do.
[31:45] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): And the edge cases must be tested, not the average. The business pain is always in the unusual ten percent.
[31:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Agreed. Decision process — who's actually involved?
[32:00] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Enterprise applications sponsors, which is me. Then the architecture board, information security, the works council for some workflow monitoring use cases, procurement, and regional IT.
[32:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's six.
[32:18] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That is six. Welcome to DeltaWorks.
[32:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): In what order?
[32:24] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Architecture board first, and that is the one that matters. If architecture says no, nothing else happens. Information security runs in parallel. The works council only if the use case requires it, which is why Anika wanted it discussed today. Procurement last, and slowly.
[32:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And who can say no unilaterally?
[32:51] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Architecture board and information security. Regional IT cannot say no formally but can make implementation impossible, which amounts to the same thing.
[33:04] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a very useful distinction and I appreciate you making it.
[33:09] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I have watched vendors ignore regional IT and I have watched what happens to them.
[33:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Noted. Timing?
[33:19] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Formal architecture review in September. Procurement in Q4. Realistic production use early next year.
[33:29] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Early next year.
[33:31] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I know that is slow for you.
[33:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's slow, but it's honest, and a slow honest timeline is worth more to me than a fast invented one. I've had Q3 dates that turned into the following June.
[33:47] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Ours will not turn into the following June. It may turn into March.
[33:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] I'll take March.
[33:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What has to be true to move from where we are to a decision?
[34:02] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): The architecture has to be viable. Specifically SAP and the on-premise systems. If the answer is "possible but requires nine months of integration work", then the first use case is too heavy and we should choose a different first use case or not proceed.
[34:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the crux, isn't it.
[34:26] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That is the crux. Honestly — the biggest issue is whether SAP and our on-premise systems make the implementation too heavy for the first use case. Everything else is manageable.
[34:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the alternative?
[34:45] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): MuleSoft and custom integration services. We already own MuleSoft. If someone can demonstrate that the business-owned workflow layer can be built on top of it acceptably, that is the cheaper path even if it is the worse one.
[35:04] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is that a real possibility or a procurement position?
[35:09] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): [pause] It is a real possibility. I do not think it is a good idea, because it makes every workflow change an integration project, which is the problem we are trying to solve. But it is a real possibility and someone will propose it.
[35:29] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let's make sure the architecture note addresses it directly rather than pretending it isn't the alternative.
[35:37] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Yes. Please do that.
[35:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Direct question. What's the next step?
[35:45] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): I will be honest with you. I see strategic potential here. But I do not think a sandbox is the next step.
[35:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me why, because I want to make sure I've understood.
[35:59] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Because a sandbox would show me the product works, and I already believe the product works. It would not tell me whether we can deploy it, and that is the open question. If I give a sandbox to my team they will spend three weeks building something impressive and we will be no closer to knowing whether SAP connectivity is viable.
[36:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a completely coherent argument and I'd rather you made it than humoured me.
[36:31] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): So — send us the architecture material first. The deployment patterns, the on-premise connectivity options, the SAP integration routes with honest difficulty ratings. Then we determine whether the deployment model is viable. If it is, we talk about a sandbox and a pilot. If it is not, we stop and neither of us has wasted a quarter.
[36:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Agreed. Jon, what do you need from Martin to produce that?
[37:05] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The list of specific SAP operations for the candidate use case. Your promotion process documentation. And an hour with whoever owns the SAP interfaces. With those I can produce something with substance rather than a marketing architecture diagram.
[37:24] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): You will have all three by the end of next week.
[37:29] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then I'll come back within two weeks of receiving them.
[37:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And I'll send the security pack in parallel — SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, DR documentation, pen test material. Plus Jon's note on team-level versus individual-level visibility for the works council question.
[37:56] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Do not forget that note. Anika will ask.
[38:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I won't forget it.
[38:04] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): There is one more thing I want to say and then we should finish.
[38:09] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go ahead.
[38:11] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Some of what we told you today was approximate. The thirty-one scripts is a count from an audit that was not exhaustive. The mismatch cost I could not give you a number for. The two German plants — I said they are prohibited from exposing production databases, and I believe that is correct, but I have not read the actual policy in eighteen months.
[38:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's exactly the sort of thing I need to know.
[38:42] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): So when you write your summary, please separate what we confirmed from what we estimated. I have seen approximations become requirements and then become the reason a project failed.
[38:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll send a written recap with open questions in a separate column from confirmed requirements. And I'll list the things I heard as estimates so you can correct them.
[39:11] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Then we understand each other.
[39:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me summarise. The opportunity is a business-owned workflow layer above MuleSoft, not a replacement for it. The first candidate is contract close to SAP validation to ServiceNow tasks, with early mismatch escalation. The decisive question is deployment architecture, specifically SAP and on-premise connectivity, and until that's answered nothing else matters. Governance requires the full security pack plus a works council position on individual-level visibility. And the next step is architecture material, not a sandbox.
[39:56] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): That is an accurate summary. I am mildly surprised.
[40:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] I'll take mildly surprised.
[40:05] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): It is high praise from me.
[40:08] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): One last thing from me, if there's time.
[40:12] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Quickly.
[40:14] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Rate limiting. You mentioned SAP. If there's a downstream quota or a throttling constraint on any of these systems, give me the actual number rather than "it's sensitive to load", because high-volume behaviour should be tested against a real limit.
[40:33] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): There is a constraint on one of the SQL Server systems. I will find the number.
[40:40] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Thank you. That's the kind of thing that surfaces in week eight otherwise.
[40:46] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): Understood. Right. Thank you both. This was more useful than I expected.
[40:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thank you, Martin. And if you remember the vendor from Hannover, do tell me.
[40:59] Martin Vogel (Director of Enterprise Applications, DeltaWorks Manufacturing): [laughs] I will. Goodbye.
[41:03] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Bye.
[41:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Bye.
